subject: Qualification recap & KPI / ops roadmap for Redwood pilot
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Lin <sasha@orchidai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Qualification recap & KPI / ops roadmap for Redwood pilot

Hi Sasha — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed ops/KPI roadmap to keep momentum. I kept this intentionally short so we can paste into the MAP.

Call highlights (from Redwood side):
- Primary goal: Replace current embed + retrieval pipeline for customer support summarization with a lower-latency, lower-cost inference path while maintaining answer accuracy.
- Preferred deployment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) for the pilot; we agreed to validate both latency & token economics.

Proposed success criteria (measurement approach in parentheses):
- Latency: p95 < 500ms end-to-end for 1k-token prompt (measured at client-side + server timing).
- Throughput: steady-state 80–120 RPS for typical burst profile; validate with 10m sustained window (use load profile attached).
- Cost: target cost/token <= $0.0008 (billing simulation vs real tokens; include cache-hit adjustments).
- Quality: maintain F1-like relevance on our 5k curated test prompts; hallucination rate < 2% (evaluated with the evaluation-metrics.md we attach).

Operational checkpoints & owners:
- Week 0 (this week): Agree mutual-action-plan (MAP) template and data access. Owner: Sasha (PM) + Hannah.
- Week 1: Sandbox deployment + sample traffic (Redwood infra + Orchid sample dataset). Owner: Ben Carter (Redwood eng) + Orchid infra.
- Week 2: Run acceptance harness (latency, throughput, cost analysis, quality eval). Owner: Monica Patel (Redwood CS) + Orchid data scientist.
- Week 3: Readout and go/no-go decision; discuss dedicated capacity if pass. Owners: Hannah + Sasha.

Immediate next steps (tracked in HubSpot):
1) Hannah: share MAP template and load profile today. (Attachment: Redwood_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx)
2) Sasha: confirm sample dataset location and any redaction constraints by EOD Friday.
3) Ben: validate instrumentation hooks we’ll need (tracing, per-token cost export).

Notes / risks:
- Data privacy: Orchid asked about PII redaction and KV-cache persistence. We will provide our data retention and KMS integration doc separately; can loop in security if needed.
- Warm cache behavior will materially affect p95 — we’ll design the harness to capture cold vs warm windows.

Attachment: Redwood_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (spreadsheet template)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m sync Wednesday if that helps.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — this is really helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Timeline: Week 0–3 works; our legal/compliance review will run in parallel and could take up to 10 business days.
- Data: we'll provide a 20k-record subset with synthetic PII for the initial sandbox. Exact S3 path by Friday.
- Quality metric: we use a blended metric (Answer Accuracy + Source Attribution) — happy to map this to your evaluation doc.

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm whether the KV cache is persisted between requests on Dedicated nodes and how that affects billing?
2) We need a short statement on SOC 2 controls for the trial (our security team will likely request it).

Cc'ing Ben for instrumentation details and Monica once we have the dataset.

Best,

sasha@orchidai.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Lin <sasha@orchidai.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification recap & KPI / ops roadmap for Redwood pilot

Hi Sasha — quick technical follow-up on the KV/cache and instrumentation points.

Short answers:
- KV cache: on Redwood Dedicated the KV cache is process-local; it will persist for the lifetime of the serving process but not as a long-term DB. For the pilot, we can enable a warm-start phase and measure both cold-start and warm p95 independently; billing is token-based plus a small reserved pool charge for Dedicated capacity during the pilot window.
- SOC2: I'll attach a short controls note and can share an FAQ; for full evidence we typically run an encrypted artifact transfer via our security channel.

Evaluation / instrumentation specifics (what we need from Orchid):
- Tracing headers on each request (x-request-id) and a short mapping file to join request IDs to sample IDs.
- Two traffic profiles: "support-burst" (high QPS, short prompts) and "doc-summarize" (lower QPS, longer prompts). I attached a sample load profile and an evaluation checklist.

Acceptance gates we’ll run in the harness:
- Gate A: Stability — no more than 1% error rate under the support-burst profile for 10m.
- Gate B: Latency — p95 < 500ms under steady-state; we’ll report cold vs warm.
- Gate C: Quality — blended accuracy >= 88% on your labeled subset; hallucination rate < 2%.
- Gate D: Cost — measured cost/token under test harness <= $0.0008 after cache discounting.

Attachments: orcid_load_profile.json; evaluation-metrics.md

If that looks good I’ll kick off the sandbox deploy Monday and share the instrumentation snippets you can paste into your client.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
